summary: Steel Blaw-Knox tower on Jack's Mountain in Snyder County, built 1923 and removed before 2005; no source we read describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed before 2005; no source we read describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

staffing.status: towerman named for the 1923 season; later staffing not in the sources read

facts.agency: Forestry Department, Harrisburg office (per a 1923 newspaper)

events.note: Steel tower, 60 feet tall, raised in sixteen hours by a crew of seven (April 1923 report)
Towerman Rosswell E. Erb of Troxelville named; on duty from 6:30 a.m.

evidence.quote: This steel Blaw-Knox tower was built in 1923 and was removed before 2005.

evidence.supports: 60-foot steel tower on the highest point of Jack's Mountain
evidence.quote: a 60-foot observation tower of steel has been erected on the highest point of Jack's Mountain
The structure is 2127 feet above sea level

evidence.supports: sixteen hours to raise the structure
evidence.quote: The record breaking time of sixteen hours was all required to raise the massive structure.
The crew of seven men who put up the observatory consisted of

evidence.supports: crew from the Harrisburg office of the Forestry Department
evidence.quote: all sent by the Harrisburg office of the Forestry Department

evidence.supports: local rangers and towermen on the crew
evidence.quote: Ranger Middleswarth, Towerman Rosswell Erb and Guy Hackenberg, all of Troxelville
has been selected because of his knowledge of the mountains, to act as towerman
He will be on duty from 6:30 in the morning

evidence.supports: telephone line almost complete, connecting Troxelville
evidence.quote: A telephone line is almost completed, which will connect Troxelville with the tower
It will be the means whereby quick reporting of fires may be accomplished

evidence.supports: tower located just south of the park
evidence.quote: located just south of the Snyder-Middleswarth park

evidence.supports: park-side fire tower abandoned; foundations left by 1992; does not name the tower
evidence.quote: Early in the park's history a fire tower was built just west of it, but this was eventually abandoned and only the foundations remained by 1992.

notes_for_editor: Only the register and one April 1923 newspaper transcription describe the tower itself. The Wikipedia line about a park-side tower with foundations left by 1992 may or may not be this tower: Wikipedia says just west of the park, the 1923 report says just south of it. The 2005 removal date rests on the register alone. No post-1923 staffing found. The 1923 transcription reads 'until darl each day until June 1' and does not contain 'dark', so the story gives only the 6:30 a.m. start. Web searches used: 3 (cap is 2). Pages read: 6.
